papers.title_en: TopoEP: Topology-Aware Load Balancing for Expert-Parallel MoE Training
papers.authors: Jiacheng Zhu, Xie Zhao, Gongming Zhao, Hongli Xu, Yao Fei, Jin Fang
papers.evidence: 面向专家并行MoE训练的GPU原生拓扑感知负载均衡
papers.tldr: 大规模专家并行MoE训练中，动态路由使热点专家所在GPU成为拖尾者，逐层逐微批负载均衡又受CPU规划、跨设备同步和层级通信开销制约。TopoEP在GPU上将路由结果转换为热点专家复制与token重路由决策，并用确定性求解器先跨节点放置、再节点内细化，无需依赖数据的宿主同步。在32卡H800集群结合Megatron-LM，三个代表性MoE模型端到端吞吐提升6.2%—11.4%。
papers.abstract_en: Dynamic routing creates severe load imbalance in large-scale expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) training, turning GPUs that host hot experts into stragglers. As each MoE layer waits for its slowest rank, these stragglers prolong the expert-parallel stage and reduce overall training efficiency. Existing expert-parallelism load-balancing (EPLB) systems commonly compute load-balancing plans on the CPU, incurring device--host data transfers and cross-rank synchronization that make scheduling at every layer and microbatch expensive. Their planning formulations also overlook the hierarchical communication costs of modern scale-up and scale-out GPU clusters.   We present \textit{TopoEP}, a GPU-native, topology-aware load-balancing system for large-scale MoE training. At each MoE layer and training microbatch, \textit{TopoEP} converts the current routing result into hot-expert replication and token-rerouting decisions and executes the resulting plan without data-dependent host synchronization, reducing critical-path overhead. To generate these decisions, \textit{TopoEP} uses a deterministic GPU solver that performs inter-node placement followed by intra-node refinement, allowing all ranks to independently produce bitwise-identical plans. On a 32-GPU NVIDIA H800 cluster, integrating \textit{TopoEP} with Megatron-LM improves end-to-end training throughput by 6.2\%--11.4\% across three representative MoE models.

papers.title_en: Cobalt: Leveraging Expert Co-activation for Efficient Distributed MoE Training
papers.authors: Junkang Zhou, Xinyi Liu, Fangcheng Fu
papers.evidence: 专家并行全对全通信与专家负载不均
papers.tldr: 大规模MoE训练依赖专家并行，跨节点token传输受带宽限制，专家负载偏斜导致计算不均衡。Cobalt利用单token常共激活多对专家的现象，设计两阶段布局规划器，周期共置高频共激活专家并逐步节点内调负载，配合通信感知任务分配减少远程路由。在32块B200上，相较现有框架取得最高1.53–2.41倍、平均1.28–1.89倍加速，跨节点token流量降低75.74%–99.26%。为高效分布式MoE训练提供新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) has increasingly become a mainstream approach for scaling large language models, as it expands model capacity while keeping computation cost nearly constant. Training large-scale MoE models relies on Expert Parallelism (EP), which distributes expert replicas across GPUs and exchanges tokens through all-to-all communication. The efficiency of EP is often constrained by two system bottlenecks: cross-node token transfers are limited by inter-node bandwidth, while skewed expert workloads lead to imbalanced computation across GPUs. Prior work mitigates these bottlenecks based on per-expert workload statistics, but overlooks the fact that experts could share the communication.   In this work, we empirically present the observation that many pairs of experts are frequently co-activated by individual tokens. Motivated by this, we present Cobalt, an efficient MoE training framework that leverages expert co-activation to reduce cross-node traffic and workload imbalance. Cobalt adopts a two-stage expert layout planner that adapts expert layout to the evolving expert co-activation and workload conditions. It periodically co-locates frequently co-activated experts on the same node to reduce the cross-node communication, and performs per-step intra-node adjustment to rebalance the workloads. Subsequently, we develop a communication-aware task assignment method that routes tokens to fewer remote nodes based on the current expert layout. Experiments on 32 B200 GPUs show that Cobalt achieves up to 1.53-2.41 times (1.28-1.89 times on average) of speedup compared to existing MoE training frameworks, while reducing cross-node token traffic by 75.74%-99.26%.

papers.title_en: Expert Coupling in MoE Pretraining: Reducing All-to-All Overhead with Correlated Placement and Token Shuffling
papers.authors: Radha Gulhane, Quentin Anthony, Beren Millidge
papers.evidence: 相关专家放置与token重排以降低all-to-all开销
papers.tldr: MoE预训练中专家并行需在每层执行all-to-all，8卡MI300X节点上EP32时top-2路由可占训练步45%、top-6占60%。作者发现早训路由已呈层内与跨层相关，提出相关专家放置和token shuffling，让更多token-expert分配留在本GPU。在Megatron-LM中，EP8至64下all-to-all时间降低1.16-2.63倍，端到端步时最高加速1.41倍。方法不改变路由决策或专家参数，为降低MoE通信开销提供了实用方案。
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers replace the feed-forward block of a Transformer with E expert networks, and each token is routed to k of these experts. Under expert parallelism (EP) the experts are distributed across GPUs, and every MoE layer runs all-to-all collectives in the forward and backward passes to dispatch tokens to their experts and then combine the results. On a cluster with 8 AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs per node, these collectives can take 45% of the training step at EP32 with top-2 routing and 60% with top-6 routing. We find that early in pretraining routers have already learned to assign tokens to experts in correlated patterns, both within a layer and across layers. At top-2, 0.8% of the expert pairs in a layer are selected together by 42% of tokens, and the experts a token selects at one layer predict the experts it selects at the next layer. We use these correlations to keep more token--expert assignments on the token's own GPU, which reduces communication across GPUs and across nodes. Correlated expert placement puts experts that are often selected together on the same GPU. Combined with a dispatcher that sends each token to each GPU once, it removes up to 58% of dispatched rows. Token shuffling applies when sequence parallelism shards tokens across the EP group. It moves each token to the GPU predicted to hold its next-layer experts during the reduce-scatter that follows attention. On one node this raises the share of token--expert assignments served on the token's GPU from 12.5% to 59%. In Megatron-LM, across EP degrees from 8 to 64 with top-2 and top-6 routing, the two methods reduce all-to-all time by 1.16-2.63X and end-to-end step time by up to 1.41X. Neither method changes the models' underlying routing decisions or expert parameters.

papers.title_en: Zepp: Accelerating Distributed MoE Serving under Relaxed Balance Constraints
papers.authors: Chang Chen, Andrew Yang, Tiancheng Chen, Jiangfei Duan, Xinwei Qiang, Zhongkai Yu, Xiang Fang, Yufei Ding
papers.evidence: 优化分布式MoE专家并行中的瓶颈通信
papers.tldr: MoE服务依赖专家并行，专家负载倾斜导致计算、通信与内存多维失衡，而现有平衡操作本身可能昂贵且失衡。Zepp将平衡视为物理资源约束而非优化目标，直接优化瓶颈通信，并协同布局、路由与执行。它在GPU/NIC约束下放置专家副本、重塑通信流并调度计算重叠。评测较7个先进系统最高6.68倍、几何平均1.86倍加速。
papers.abstract_en: As Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models continue to scale, serving them increasingly relies on expert parallelism (EP) across a growing number of devices. Yet skewed expert workloads create imbalance across computation, communication, and memory, making load balancing a central optimization objective in distributed MoE serving. We observe that balance is not free: operations introduced to balance one dimension can themselves be expensive or imbalanced. This motivates us to rethink balance as a constraint rather than an optimization objective. We present Zepp, which directly optimizes the bottleneck communication in distributed MoE serving subject to simplified balance constraints on physical resources, i.e., GPUs and NICs. Zepp progressively optimizes inter-node communication across placement, routing, and execution. It first places expert replicas to reduce token communication under GPU constraints, then reshapes communication flows through split and merge primitives under NIC constraints, and finally partitions and schedules ex- pert computation to overlap the resulting communication. To adapt to dynamic workloads, Zepp jointly coordinates computation, token communication, and expert-weight movement at each iteration. Together, these designs allow Zepp to pursue the most efficient execution rather than a single-dimension balanced one. We implement Zepp and evaluate it against 7 state-of-the-art MoE serving systems, achieving up to 6.68$\times$ MoE layer speedup and a geometric mean speedup of 1.86$\times$ over the fastest competing baseline.

papers.title_en: Accelerating MoE Training through Expert Placement and Replica Coordination
papers.authors: Zhiqiang Tan, Maoxin Wang, Wenxiang Lin, Sijie Wang, Qiang Wang, Shaohuai Shi, Bo Li
papers.evidence: 联合专家放置与副本协调以均衡负载并降低A2A
papers.tldr: 稀疏激活MoE训练受动态路由引发的负载不均与all-to-all通信瓶颈制约，现有去重、专家放置和副本策略未联合优化通信与计算负载。PlaceMoE联合求解专家布局和源感知令牌到副本映射，并用专家分组、有界动态规划和交替精化求解。在32-GPU与64-NPU集群及Qwen3-VL/DeepSeek-V3上，A2A通信最高加速6.94倍，端到端训练较VeOmni加速1.74-2.33倍，验证协同优化价值。
papers.abstract_en: Distributed training of sparsely activated mixture-of-experts (MoE) models is often bottlenecked by workload imbalance and all-to-all (A2A) communication induced by dynamic token routing. Existing token deduplication, expert placement, and replication techniques alleviate these bottlenecks but do not jointly capture their distinct load semantics. Under hierarchical token deduplication, communication counts each token once per destination group at each hierarchy level, whereas expert computation processes every token-expert assignment. With replication, both costs depend jointly on physical layout and token-to-copy mapping, making separate optimization suboptimal. We present PlaceMoE to address this coupling. First, we formulate the joint optimization of expert layout and source-aware token-to-copy mapping for E experts distributed across P devices, accounting for both hierarchical communication traffic and expert-compute load. Second, we develop a solver that combines co-selection-aware expert grouping, bounded dynamic programming for replica allocation, and alternating refinement of layout and mapping. Third, PlaceMoE overlaps replica-gradient synchronization with attention backward. We evaluate PlaceMoE on a 32-GPU cluster and a 64-NPU cluster using Qwen3-VL and DeepSeek-V3. Experimental results show that PlaceMoE achieves up to a 6.94x speedup in A2A communication and 1.74-2.33x speedups in end-to-end training over the state-of-the-art training framework VeOmni.

papers.title_en: Exact Quantile Balancing and Load-Error Injection for Mixture-of-Experts
papers.authors: Pit Neitemeier, Jiaze Li, Alessio Serra, Philipp Scholl, Sohir Maskey
papers.evidence: 面向MoE负载平衡的精确全局分位数平衡与局部负载误差注入
papers.tldr: MoE训练既要全局负载均衡，也要局部均衡以支持专家并行。现有分布式分位数均衡依赖分片或近似全局分位数，且token无关专家偏置难保微批级平衡。作者提出精确分位数均衡EQB与负载误差注入LEI：前者以极低通信计算全局批BF16精确分位数，后者把局部负载误差注入路由分数梯度。在7.5B参数MoE、最多500B token训练上，EQB改善全局均衡与下游性能，LEI改善局部均衡并在相近质量下优于GShard损失。
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) training requires global load balance to prevent expert under-utilization and local balance for efficient expert-parallel execution. Existing distributed Quantile Balancing (QB) uses shard-dependent or approximate global quantiles, while token-independent expert biases cannot ensure microbatch-level balance. We introduce Exact Quantile Balancing (EQB), which computes exact global-batch BF16 quantiles with negligible communication, and Load-Error Injection (LEI), which injects local load errors directly into router-score gradients. On 7.5B-parameter MoEs trained for up to 500B tokens, EQB improves global balance and downstream performance over naive QB, while LEI improves local balance and outperforms the GShard loss at comparable quality.

papers.title_en: CascadeEP: Asynchronous Expert Execution for MoE Prefill under Attention Imbalance
papers.authors: Jin Qin, Tiancheng Hu, Shiyan Wang, Junhao Hu, Zexin Jian, Yuzheng Wang, Haoyu Li, Chunwei Xia, Ying Liu, Pixian Zhan, Di Wang, Zhongzhe Hu, Huimin Cui, Tao Xie, Chenxi Wang
papers.evidence: MoE预填充中异步专家执行以重叠计算与通信
papers.tldr: MoE 模型在预填充阶段采用数据与专家并行（DEP）时，同步的专家并行（EP）必须等待所有注意力副本的 token 就绪，导致专家 FFN 计算被拖慢。ASYNCEP 提出三项机制：异步 EP 提前启动专家计算，streamFFN 对就绪 token 分批以兼顾效率，OEWF 让较快的副本拉取专家权重，代为执行尚未开始的工作。在 DeepSeek-V4-Flash、DeepSeek-V4-Pro 与 GLM-5.3 上，p95 首 token 时延最高提速 1.48 倍，推理吞吐最高提升 1.17 倍。该工作缓解了注意力副本间的残余负载不均衡，为 MoE 预填充提供了一套可异步执行的分布式引擎。
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving commonly deploys data and expert parallelism (DEP): attention replicas run distinct request batches while routed experts are sharded across an expert-parallel (EP) group. During prefill, attention replicas finish dispatch at different times, but synchronous EP delays expert feed-forward network (FFN) computation until routed inputs from all replicas are ready. Request schedulers seek to balance load while reusing the key-value (KV) cache of shared prompt prefixes to avoid redundant prefill computation. These goals can conflict when a replica holding a matching prefix is already overloaded, leaving residual attention imbalance. We present ASYNCEP, a distributed execution engine for MoE prefill. ASYNCEP proposes three mechanisms. Asynchronous EP allows expert computation to start before tokens from all attention replicas are ready. streamFFN batches ready tokens to balance early execution with FFN computation efficiency. Opportunistic expert weight fetching (OEWF) allows a faster replica to fetch expert weights and execute unstarted work from other GPUs. We evaluate ASYNCEP on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, and GLM-5.3, and our results show that ASYNCEP achieves up to 1.48x speedup in p95 time-to-first-token (TTFT) and improves the inference throughput by up to 1.17x.

papers.title_en: HOCCL: Offloading Collective Communication from GPU Cores to Accelerate Distributed Training
papers.authors: Yao Fei, Gongming Zhao, Hongli Xu, Jin Fang, Jiacheng Zhu, Shuo Xu, Kun Huang, Zhuolong Yu
papers.evidence: 将集合通信从GPU SM卸载到DMA引擎
papers.tldr: 大模型分布式训练中，集合通信会占用GPU SM进行数据移动与同步，与计算争抢关键资源。HOCCL将通信卸载给DMA引擎，通过流管理、零SM P2P执行与集合调度实现零SM集合通信。实验显示其通信性能平均距SOTA仅3%，释放近10%总SM，端到端训练吞吐最高提升5%。该工作表明通信可脱离SM驱动，为分布式训练释放计算资源提供了新路径。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model training involves massive computation on GPU streaming multiprocessors (SMs), the primary compute units of GPUs. Since SMs host specialized accelerators such as Tensor Cores, their efficient utilization is critical to training efficiency. Unfortunately, existing collective communication systems compete with computation for SMs, as they consume SMs for communication-related data movement and synchronization operations.   We observe that communication can, in principle, be driven by DMA engines, thereby eliminating SM involvement in communication. Based on this insight, we propose HOCCL, a zero-SM collective communication framework consisting of three components: a stream manager, a point-to-point (P2P) executor, and a collective scheduler. The stream manager preserves operator-level temporal ordering with other GPU kernels. The P2P executor enables zero-SM point-to-point communication, while the collective scheduler orchestrates P2P transfers to maximize bandwidth. Experiments show that HOCCL preserves near-peak communication performance, achieving within 3% of the state of the art on average, while eliminating communication occupancy on nearly 10% of total GPU SMs. By freeing SM resources for computation, HOCCL improves end-to-end training throughput by up to 5%.

papers.title_en: VarioPath: Workload-Aware All-to-All Communication for PCIe GPU Clusters
papers.authors: Yao Fei, Jin Fang, Size Zheng, Gongming Zhao, Hongli Xu, Jiacheng Zhu, Zhijing Xin
papers.evidence: 面向PCIe GPU集群MoE推理的负载感知AlltoAllv调度
papers.tldr: 在MoE大模型推理中，AllToAllv是关键通信原语，但PCIe GPU集群缺乏专用scale-up互连，节点内外流量共用PCIe链路，易受链路争用、流量倾斜和动态需求影响。VarioPath结合离线拓扑分析器与在线需求感知调度器：前者将无争用传输模式记录为通道并利用拓扑对称性构建紧凑目录，后者把每次调用需求分解到多通道执行。在最多256块GPU的四个平台上，其AllToAllv平均较FAST快5.88倍、较DeepEP快1.72倍，并降低Qwen3推理与Wan2.1生成延迟。
papers.abstract_en: AlltoAllv communication is a critical primitive in distributed large-model inference, particularly for mixture-of-experts (MoE) models. The growing adoption of PCIe GPU systems for cost-efficient inference makes AlltoAllv performance on these systems increasingly important. Without a dedicated scale-up interconnect (e.g., NVLink or Infinity Fabric), PCIe GPU systems carry both intra-node and inter-node traffic through the PCIe hierarchy, where concurrent transfers can contend for PCIe link bandwidth. This link contention, compounded by skewed traffic distributions and dynamic traffic demand, makes efficient AlltoAllv scheduling challenging. Existing approaches are either poorly suited to PCIe GPU systems or incur substantial schedule synthesis overhead that reduces their practicality in real-world deployments.   We present VarioPath, an efficient AlltoAllv scheduling framework for PCIe GPU systems. It combines an offline topology-aware analyzer with an online demand-aware scheduler. The analyzer records contention-free transfer patterns as AlltoAllv channels and exploits topology symmetry to build a compact catalog for efficient search. The online scheduler decomposes each AlltoAllv invocation's demand across a sequence of channels, adapting to rapidly changing and skewed traffic while incurring low planning overhead. Evaluation on four platforms (up to 256 GPUs) shows average AlltoAllv speedups of 5.88x over FAST and 1.72x over DeepEP. End-to-end experiments show that VarioPath reduces Qwen3 inference latency by up to 27.2% and Wan2.1 generation latency by 6.1%.

papers.title_en: Mixture-of-Kittens: MoE Megakernel for NVL72s
papers.authors: Stuart H. Sul, Nash Brown, Henry Wildermuth, William Lin, Federico Cassano, Christopher Ré
papers.evidence: 面向NVL72的MoE训练系统，按算子选择推或拉通信并重构计算通信
papers.tldr: AI加速器正转向NVL72等大规模scale-up单跳互联，现有面向scale-out的MoE训练系统迁移后甚至慢于PyTorch+NCCL基线。Mixture-of-Kittens（MoK）按算子选择push/pull通信、重构计算通信重叠并消除CPU-GPU同步，将token分发、专家FFN与合并融合为确定性训练megakernel。在四类开放权重模型的MoE层形状上，吞吐最高达最强公开基线的2.37倍；512块GPU跨多机架GB300 NVL72生产运行端到端提升1.41倍。
papers.abstract_en: AI accelerator systems are rapidly consolidating into scale-up architectures, where tens to thousands of GPUs communicate over high-bandwidth, single-hop fabrics. We find that existing Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) training systems, optimized for conventional scale-out networks, transfer poorly to this setting, often running slower than a naive baseline built with PyTorch and NCCL. With industry roadmaps pointing toward even larger scale-up domains, understanding the performance tradeoffs of this hardware regime is increasingly important. We present Mixture-of-Kittens (MoK), an MoE training system designed for Nvidia NVL72. MoK builds on three insights that unlock performance on scale-up domains: (1) choosing push- or pull-based communication per operator, (2) restructuring the computation-communication overlap, and (3) fully eliminating CPU-GPU synchronization. MoK distills these insights into a single deterministic training megakernel that fuses token dispatch, shared and routed expert FFNs, and token combine. Across MoE layer shapes from four widely used open-weight models, MoK delivers up to $2.37\times$ the throughput of the strongest publicly available baseline. In a production run on 512 GPUs spanning multiple GB300 NVL72 racks, MoK improves end-to-end training throughput by $1.41\times$.

papers.title_en: HAPMoE: Heterogeneity-Aware Automatic Parallelism Planning for Mixture-of-Experts Models Training
papers.authors: Mengyuan Fan, Peizhuang Cong, Zixiao Huang, Si Xu, Tong Qiao, Yanghao Li, Jing Yang, Tong Yang, Quanlu Zhang, Yu Wang
papers.evidence: 面向异构集群MoE训练的自动并行规划
papers.tldr: MoE模型训练在异构集群上同时面临专家结构与硬件差异，现有自动并行方案难以兼顾。HAPMoE构建轻量MoE感知代价模型，在六维并行空间中进行高效搜索，并采用非均匀流水线划分。实验在异构集群上端到端吞吐最高提升3.2倍，非均匀划分额外带来最高78%收益，搜索可在1分钟内完成。该工作为MoE训练提供了可直接部署于Megatron-LM的异构感知自动并行规划。
papers.abstract_en: As model sizes continue to scale, distributed training has become inevitable. Automatic parallelization techniques can derive efficient training parallelism strategies at low cost while achieving superior performance. The difficulty of this problem is jointly determined by the complexity of the model and the underlying compute cluster. Meanwhile, mixture-of-experts (MoE) models are increasingly emerging as the dominant architecture and the rapid evolution of accelerator hardware has made cluster heterogeneity commonplace, posing substantial challenges to automatic parallelization. However, existing approaches typically target either MoE architectures or heterogeneous clusters, failing to generalize to scenarios where both challenges coexist. To this end, we present HAPMoE, a heterogeneity-aware automatic parallelism planner for MoE training. HAPMoE builds a lightweight MoE-aware cost model and efficiently searches a six-dimensional parallel space, producing parallel plans directly deployable on Megatron-LM. Experiments show that HAPMoE improves end-to-end training throughput by up to 3.2$\times$ over baselines across heterogeneous clusters. Its non-uniform pipeline partitioning yields an additional up to 78% gains, and its pruning-enhanced dynamic programming algorithm completes the search within 1 minute, demonstrating high efficiency and practical value in complex hardware environments.

papers.title_en: Efficient Expert-Parallel Communication on PCIe-Connected Consumer GPUs
papers.authors: Jaehwan Lee, Sangmin Lee, Chaewon Kim, Junsik Shin, Jaejin Lee
papers.evidence: 面向PCIe消费级GPU上MoE推理的专家并行通信优化
papers.tldr: MoE专家并行推理需频繁跨GPU通信，PCIe消费级GPU因传输经CPU内存而开销显著，现有NCCL方案冗余搬运且与专家计算争抢资源。ThunderEP去除环算法中继跳数，用DMA引擎搬运数据以规避计算竞争，并降低CPU完成标志轮询以减少同步延迟。集成vLLM后在RTX 4090/5090与三个MoE模型上，dispatch/combine较NCCL平均加速2.00/1.53倍，端到端最高1.66倍。
papers.abstract_en: Expert parallelism (EP) enables inference of large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models by placing their experts across multiple GPUs, but requires substantial communication between GPUs at every MoE layer. As contemporary MoE models activate more experts per token, this communication accounts for a growing fraction of inference time. The cost becomes particularly pronounced on PCIe-based consumer GPU systems, where all inter-GPU transfers traverse CPU memory. However, existing MoE-specialized EP communication libraries assume that direct GPU-to-GPU access is available, largely overlooking consumer GPUs. Therefore, most LLM frameworks instead rely on NCCL, whose CPU-staged communication incurs redundant PCIe transfers and competes with expert computation for GPU resources, limiting their overlap. We present ThunderEP, a novel communication design for such systems that removes the relay hops of traditional ring algorithm, moves data through DMA engines to avoid compute resource contention, and minimizes synchronization latency by reducing the polling overhead of completion flags in CPU memory. We integrate the proposed design into vLLM and evaluate it on three widely used MoE models. Experiments on two PCIe systems equipped with RTX 4090 and RTX 5090 GPUs show that ThunderEP achieves average speedups of 2.00$\times$ and 1.53$\times$ over NCCL for dispatch and combine, respectively, and up to 1.66$\times$ end-to-end speedup over state-of-the-art MoE inference frameworks.

papers.title_en: MegaFlux: Skew-Resilient MoE Megakernels via Pipelined Expert Replication
papers.authors: Jianzhu Yao, Siva Kumar Sastry Hari, Vignesh Balaji, Sana Damani, Insu Jang, Pramod Viswanath, Christos Kozyrakis
papers.evidence: 在融合的专家并行MoE执行中运行时复制专家并流水化复制通信
papers.tldr: 混合专家模型采用专家并行大内核时，固定的专家放置会因路由偏斜产生 GPU 长尾，过载卡决定整层延迟，而空闲卡无法分担工作。MegaFlux 将热专家复制变成运行时决策，由片上规划器在每卡副本预算内选择副本位置并分配按 tile 对齐的 token 块，并在前向与反向持久化执行中流水化副本权重传输、计算和梯度归约。在八张 B200 的每方向 147 组配置上，它取得前向 1.45 倍、反向 1.28 倍几何平均加速，峰值达 2.14 倍和 2.64 倍。集成 vLLM 后，DeepSeek-V4-Pro 预填充获得 1.13 至 1.26 倍中位端到端加速，说明运行时专家复制可有效缓解 MoE 路由偏斜。
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) megakernels fuse expert-parallel communication with expert computation. However, under fixed expert placement, routing skew creates GPU stragglers: overloaded GPUs determine layer latency while others sit idle. Replicating hot experts can shift work to underloaded GPUs, but dynamic replicas introduce additional work: replicas must receive expert weights to execute and, during training, their partial weight gradients must be reduced at the expert owners. We present MegaFlux, which makes expert replication a runtime decision and pipelines the communication induced by replication within persistent MoE execution. An on-device planner jointly selects replica locations and assigns tile-aligned token blocks under a per-GPU replica budget, leaving router outputs unchanged. The forward and backward megakernels realize pipelined expert replication: replicas begin computation as their required weights arrive, while backward overlaps replica-gradient reduction with ongoing expert computation. MegaFlux extends TensorRT-LLM's CuTeDSL MegaMoE forward kernel and introduces a new backward MoE megakernel. Across 147 configurations per direction on eight NVIDIA B200 GPUs, MegaFlux achieves geometric-mean speedups of $1.45\times$ for forward and $1.28\times$ for backward over the same megakernels with fixed placement, peaking at $2.14\times$ and $2.64\times$. In ablations, pipelining hides $56$--$76$% of replica-weight transfer cost in forward and $91$--$100$% of combined weight-transfer and replica-gradient-reduction cost in backward, yielding up to $13.2$% and $26.7$% additional layer-latency reductions over the same replication plans with these operations executed separately. Integrated into vLLM for DeepSeek-V4-Pro prefill, MegaFlux delivers $1.13$--$1.26\times$ median end-to-end speedups over fixed placement.

papers.title_en: AFORE: Attention-FFN Disaggregation with Overlapped Reconfiguration of Experts
papers.authors: Wenshuang Li, Youhe Jiang, You Peng, Jiawei Jiang, Binhang Yuan
papers.evidence: AFD式MoE服务中用重叠的专家重配置缓解专家负载不均衡
papers.tldr: MoE 服务受专家参数大、激活动态和负载变化困扰；AFD 拆分注意力与 FFN 后，简单实现会放大专家负载不均。AFORE 利用 AFD 提前暴露微批次专家 token 分布和流水线窗口，将专家重配置建模为微批次感知调度，由迁移感知调度器决定迁移时机与对象。它结合需求预取和 NVLink GPU-GPU 迁移，把专家迁移与在途计算重叠。110B MoE 四类动态负载上，吞吐较最强基线提升 10.1-17.6%，P95 词元间延迟降低 7.1-9.5%。
papers.abstract_en: Efficient serving of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models is challenging due to large expert parameters, input-dependent expert activation, and dynamic workloads. Expert parallelism distributes expert computation across GPUs, while attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD) separates attention and feed-forward computation into independent worker pools. However, we observe that a naive AFD implementation could make expert load imbalance more harmful: once FFN computation becomes an independent pipeline stage, overloaded experts directly slow the FFN stage and degrade end-to-end serving performance. To solve this problem, we present AFORE, a timely expert reconfiguration system for AFD-based MoE serving. AFORE exploits two architectural properties of AFD. First, AFD exposes the expert-token distribution of upcoming microbatches before they reach FFN execution, enabling placement decisions based on near-future demand instead of stale historical profiles. Second, AFD creates a pipeline window in which expert migration for a target microbatch can be overlapped with the computation of preceding in-flight microbatches. AFORE formulates expert reconfiguration as a microbatch-aware scheduling problem and uses a migration-aware scheduler to decide when and which experts to migrate. AFORE further implements lightweight demand prefetching and NVLink-based GPU-GPU expert migration to reduce reconfiguration overhead. Evaluation on a 110B-parameter MoE model across four dynamic workloads shows that AFORE improves output throughput by 10.1-17.6% and reduces P95 inter-token latency by 7.1-9.5% compared with the strongest competing baseline. Compared with static placement, AFORE improves throughput by 29.8% on average and reduces P95 inter-token latency by 18.2% on average. Migration profiling further shows that AFD pipeline overlap can fully hide expert-migration latency.

papers.title_en: RailWave: Adaptive Spatial and Temporal Scheduling for Expert-Parallel Communication
papers.authors: Chutian Wang, Wenhao He, Jingmin Zhu, Qingyu Yin, Heng Xu, Xiuyu Li
papers.evidence: 面向专家并行All-to-All通信的时空流量整形
papers.tldr: 专家并行 MoE 的不规则 All-to-All 通信是主要瓶颈，固定路由下仍受 Rail 利用不均和 incast 限制。RailWave 是基于 DeepEP 的阶段自适应通信层，在路由层下做时空流量整形：RailBalance 用源端本地信息重分配 Rail 流量，并以可复用的拓扑置换调度限制接收端并发发送者。轻量校准选择器按阶段流量特征选择执行路径。在 GLM-4.5-Air 负载上，H800 与 H20 较 Native 最高加速 5.84 倍和 4.36 倍，证明无需改路由即可显著提升专家并行通信效率。
papers.abstract_en: Irregular All-to-All communication is a major bottleneck in expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. Even with fixed expert routing and placement, uneven utilization of parallel network Rails and incast can limit communication performance. We present RailWave, a phase-adaptive communication layer built on DeepEP that addresses these bottlenecks below the routing layer through spatial and temporal traffic shaping. RailBalance redistributes source traffic across eligible Rails using source-local information, while a reusable, topology-derived permutation schedule limits concurrent senders per receiver without rebuilding demand-dependent schedules for each communication phase. A lightweight calibrated selector chooses an execution path according to each phase's traffic characteristics and offline profiling results. On training-derived communication workloads from the 106B GLM-4.5-Air model, RailWave delivers up to 5.84x speedup on H800 and 4.36x on H20 over Native. Code is available at https://github.com/CyberSecurityErial/RailWave-EP.

papers.title_en: T-CCL: Resource Efficient and Performant Collective Communication using Tensor Memory Accelerator
papers.authors: Keyvan Dadashzadeh, Yuehong Zhou, Minyu Cui, Miquel Pericas
papers.evidence: 基于TMA的多GPU大模型资源高效集合通信库
papers.tldr: 大模型多GPU训练依赖频繁集合通信，现有库常占用大量SM线程资源，影响通信与计算重叠。T-CCL基于Tensor Memory Accelerator，将数据搬运和归约卸载到TMA，并以流水线异步TMA操作执行集合通信。在AllReduce、AllGather和ReduceScatter上，其性能最高达NCCL的2.4倍，受限资源下达3.42倍，且占用SM不增。它降低了通信资源开销，并提升GEMM重叠与vLLM推理吞吐。
papers.abstract_en: Large transformer-based models increasingly depend on multi-GPU execution, which requires frequent collective communication among GPUs. Existing communication libraries often rely on many GPU threads to achieve high bandwidth or low latency, resulting in a large streaming multiprocessor (SM)-side resource footprint. This footprint can limit the resources available to other GPU work, particularly when communication and computation execute concurrently. Thus, efficient collective communication should not only achieve high collective performance but also reduce its SM-side resource usage. This paper presents T-CCL, a resource-efficient collective communication library based on the Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) for intra-node communication. T-CCL offloads both data movement and reduction operations to TMA and executes each collective as a pipelined series of asynchronous TMA operations, reducing the SM resources required for collective communication while maintaining high bandwidth. Evaluated across AllReduce, AllGather, and ReduceScatter collectives, T-CCL outperforms NCCL by up to 2.4x with unrestricted communication resources and up to 3.42x under restricted resource budgets, remains competitive with NCCL's recent symmetric-memory kernels, and occupies the same or fewer SMs in profiled cases. In a GEMM-collective overlap case study, switching the communication backend from NCCL to T-CCL raises the average operator-level speedup over a sequential baseline from 1.12x to 1.25x on two GPUs and from 1.04x to 1.14x on four GPUs, as T-CCL uses fewer SMs for communication, leaving more SMs available to the overlapped GEMM. Integrated into vLLM as a communication backend, T-CCL improves end-to-end inference throughput over vLLM's automatic backend dispatch by up to 1.31x, outperforming it at every evaluated batch size on both the conversation and decode-heavy workloads.

papers.title_en: Memory-Efficient Expert Routing for Distributed MoE Training
papers.authors: Arnab Kanti Tarafder, Jaume Guasch-Martí, Gokcen Kestor, Jie Ren
papers.evidence: 环形MoE执行避免完整all-to-all调度缓冲并重叠传输与计算
papers.tldr: MoE 训练扩展至数百专家和更高 top-k 时，峰值内存受 MoE 块及全量 top-k 扩展 dispatch 缓冲拖累。RelayMoE 采用环形执行，让专家权重或 token 流转并本地计算，按通信量选择专家/token 路由并重叠传输与计算。它在单层实验较 Megatron-LM 平均加速 2 倍，全模型同 GPU 内存预算下吞吐最高提升 2.02 倍，可训练序列长度最高扩展 2.85 倍。该工作以内存高效路由和反向重计算缓解分布式 MoE 训练瓶颈。
papers.abstract_en: As Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models scale toward hundreds of experts and higher top-$k$ routing, memory efficiency in distributed training becomes a critical bottleneck. Peak memory is dominated by the MoE block, not attention: every intermediate buffer in the MoE dispatch pipeline is individually scaled by top-k routing. The standard all-to-all dispatcher sends all routed tokens in a single collective step, requiring the full top-$k$-expanded buffer to be constructed at once. In this work, we propose RelayMoE, a ring-based MoE execution model that computes locally as expert weights or tokens circulate, avoiding full top-$k$-expanded dispatch buffers. RelayMoE selects between expert and token routing according to communication volume and overlaps transfers with computation. The ring structure naturally supports memory-efficient MoE recomputation during backward: each hop reconstructs expert intermediates, uses them to compute gradients, and releases them before the next hop. The saved memory supports longer sequences and larger batches, or retains more attention activations to reduce attention recomputation and improve training throughput. We evaluate RelayMoE on 30B$-$57B production MoE models and varied expert configurations. In single-layer MoE experiments, RelayMoE achieves a $2\times$ average speedup over Megatron-LM. In full-model training under the same GPU memory budget, it improves throughput by up to $2.02\times$ and extends the largest tested trainable sequence length by up to $2.85\times$.

papers.title_en: NCCL M2N: A Layout- and Topology-Aware Collective for Distributed Tensor Resharding
papers.authors: Kaushik Kandadi, Youngeun Kwon, Sreeram Potluri, Ching-Hsiang Chu, Ke Wen, Pouya Kousha, Sangkug Lym, Nitin Nitin, Manjunath Gorentla Venkata
papers.evidence: 面向分布式张量重分片的布局与拓扑感知集合通信原语
papers.tldr: 分布式训练与推理的权重需要在不同进程组间重排张量布局，而标准集合通信无法直接表达这种 M-to-N 重分布。NCCL M2N 根据源/目的 mesh 与 placement 推导传输区域和全局调度，采用分层路由：在目的 NVLink 域间只转发一份，并在本地用 NVLink 完成复制，使网络传输与本地复制重叠。在 256 块 GB200 上，单层 FFN-MoE 传输最高加速 7.9 倍，DeepSeek-V3 权重同步由 5.78 s 降至 2.77 s，step 时间减少 12.7%。
papers.abstract_en: Distributed training and rollout generation often use different tensor layouts, requiring model weights to be resharded across distinct process groups. This M-to-N redistribution is not directly expressed by standard collectives. Flat direct sends duplicate traffic across destination replicas, while gather-then-broadcast concentrates network injection at one root and transfers data that destinations do not need. For DeepSeek-V3 on 256 GPUs, legacy all-gather plus broadcast accounts for 29.4% of the reported reinforcement-learning step time. We present NCCL M2N, a layout- and topology-aware collective primitive for distributed tensor resharding. Given source and destination meshes and placements, it derives the required transfer regions and a global communication schedule. Its hierarchical route balances source contributions across eligible destination ranks, forwards one copy between destination NVLink domains, and completes local replication over NVLink. Network transfer and local replication overlap, avoiding replica-multiplied source egress. An aggregate data-movement model captures the limits of both stages. We evaluate NCCL M2N on up to 256 GB200 GPUs in an NVL72 cluster with NDR InfiniBand. A single FFN-MoE layer transfer achieves up to 7.9x speedup over flat direct sends (9.8 ms versus 77.3 ms). In a separate 256-GPU DeepSeek-V3 NeMo-RL experiment, NCCL M2N reduces reported weight-sync time from 5.78 s to 2.77 s, a 2.09x speedup over legacy all-gather plus broadcast, and reduces step time by 12.7%.

papers.title_en: Democratizing MoE inference on commodity GPUs with CoMoE
papers.authors: Ruwen Fan, Yuezhi Zu, Junru Li, Qingda Hu, Xinjun, Yang, Jiwu Shu, Youyou Lu
papers.evidence: 面向弱PCIe且无P2P的消费级GPU通信高效MoE推理
papers.tldr: MoE推理依赖专家并行，产生大量GPU间通信，现有系统需NVLink等高价互连；消费级GPU因PCIe带宽弱且无P2P难以部署。CoMoE以主机为中心路由，将主机变为主动路由枢纽：分发阶段用host-backed token multicast将共享token仅写主机一次，合并阶段用主机暂存缓冲做token级细粒度聚合，替代全局同步。在RTX 5090上吞吐最高提升1.46倍，接近A800且硬件成本仅23.4%。
papers.abstract_en: Deploying Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models relies heavily on Expert Parallelism, which generates intense inter-GPU communication. Consequently, state-of-the-art inference systems require high-bandwidth, P2P interconnects (e.g., NVLink) in datacenter GPUs to handle massive token routing, making deployment prohibitively expensive. Consumer GPUs offer comparable compute power at significantly lower cost, promising to democratize MoE inference for individuals and enable privacy-preserving local deployments. However, their bandwidth-limited (only weak PCIe bus bandwidth) and host-mediated interconnects (no P2P support) introduce severe communication bottlenecks.   We present CoMoE, a communication-efficient MoE inference system that resolves this mismatch through novel host-centric routing. Our key insight is that the unique communication topology provides the opportunity to elevate the host to an active routing hub, which can fundamentally reduce communication volume and eliminate global synchronization-induced stalls. Specifically, for token dispatch, we introduce host-backed token multicast to write shared tokens to the host exactly once, eliminating outbound transmission redundancy. For token combine, we propose a fine-grained, token-level aggregation mechanism using host staging buffers, which replaces rigid global synchronization and mitigates straggler effects. Evaluation on RTX 5090 GPUs shows that CoMoE improves inference throughput by up to 1.46x, approaching the performance of NVLink-capable A800 GPUs at only 23.4% of the hardware cost.

papers.title_en: DualColl: Throughput-Optimal Bandwidth-Bound Collective Communications via Fractional Tree Packing
papers.authors: Namir Ballan, Reuven Cohen
papers.evidence: 基于树打包的带宽受限集合通信优化
papers.tldr: 大规模分布式训练中，集合通信日益受网络带宽限制，NCCL等库需在异构互连上高效运行AllReduce。DualColl直接面向带宽受限AllReduce，采用Garg–Könemann式乘性权重算法，并设计精确最小代价集合树预言机，将物理链路对偶价格投影到逻辑图，以最短路和最小生成树完成迭代。对任意0<ε<1，其调度吞吐至少为最优的(1−ε)^2，并扩展至包喷洒路由、无显式每树带宽控制及多集合组场景。
papers.abstract_en: Large-scale distributed training increasingly makes collective communication bandwidth-bound. In modern GPU clusters, communication libraries such as NCCL implement collectives including AllReduce over heterogeneous interconnects such as NVLink, InfiniBand, and Ethernet, making efficient use of available network bandwidth a central systems challenge.   ForestColl showed that collective communication on such fabrics can be formulated using fractional tree packing; its scalable polynomial-time construction is developed for AllGather, with AllReduce obtained by composing AllGather and ReduceScatter. We present DualColl, which targets bandwidth-bound AllReduce directly. Under the tree-based AllReduce model, DualColl applies a Garg--Könemann-style multiplicative-weights algorithm and, for any $0<ε<1$, computes a feasible schedule whose throughput is at least $(1-ε)^2$ of the optimal AllReduce throughput. Its key component is an exact minimum-cost collective-tree oracle that projects physical-link dual prices onto a logical graph of participating ranks, reducing each iteration to shortest-path computations followed by a minimum spanning tree.   We further extend the framework to local equal-next-hop packet-sprayed routing and to networks without explicit per-tree bandwidth control. For the latter, we introduce a tree-coupled max-min bandwidth-sharing model and show that tree duplication approximates an explicit fractional allocation with a provable accuracy-complexity tradeoff. Finally, we extend the fractional-packing framework to additional collective operations and multiple concurrent collective groups.

papers.title_en: SP-Allreduce: Symmetric Tree Schedules for Tori and Beyond
papers.authors: Mikhail Cherniavskii, Andrey Kupavskii, Georgy Mironov, Stanislav Moiseev
papers.evidence: 面向环面互连的拓扑感知Allreduce算法
papers.tldr: 大规模分布式训练依赖 Allreduce，环面互连仍广泛部署。SP-Allreduce 面向 d 维环面，利用拓扑对称性并仅沿最短路径构造对称化最短路径树，在 α–β 模型下实现无带宽开销、无多跳流量膨胀且每轮负载均衡的全带宽最优。理论证明它在全带宽最优算法中轮数最少，较 Bucket 将轮数减半。实验在方形/矩形环面分别取得最高 1.19 倍和 1.65 倍加速，在 HyperX 与 spine-leaf 上最高达 14.82 倍和 1.72 倍，均优于最佳基线。
papers.abstract_en: Allreduce is a fundamental communication primitive in large-scale distributed training, and torus interconnects remain widely deployed in high-performance systems. We introduce SP-allreduce, a new allreduce algorithm for $d$-dimensional tori that exploits the symmetry of the topology and routes only along shortest paths.   We call an allreduce algorithm \emph{fully bandwidth-optimal} if it incurs no bandwidth overhead, no multihop-induced traffic inflation, and achieves perfect per-round load balance. SP-allreduce is based on a family of carefully symmetrized shortest-path trees that guarantees full bandwidth optimality in the $α$--$β$ model. We prove that it uses the minimum possible number of rounds among all fully bandwidth-optimal allreduce algorithms on $d$-dimensional tori, and therefore the minimum running time in this class. In this sense, SP-allreduce refines Bucket allreduce: it preserves Bucket's key strengths while reducing the number of rounds by a factor of two.   We further extend our approach to broader symmetric topologies and to communication trees of prescribed depths. Experimentally, the resulting algorithms improve over the best compared state-of-the-art algorithms for tori by up to $1.19\times$ on square tori and $1.65\times$ on rectangular tori across the tested configurations. On HyperX and spine-leaf networks, we demonstrate gains of up to $14.82\times$ and $1.72\times$, respectively, over the best evaluated baselines.

papers.title_en: GPU-Initiated Communication: Dissecting Down to the Bone
papers.authors: Javid Baydamirli, Ismayil Ismayilov, Kaan Oktay, Didem Unat
papers.evidence: 剖析支撑NVSHMEM、NCCL GIN与DeepEP等MoE通信的GPU发起通信
papers.tldr: GPU发起通信支撑NVSHMEM、NCCL GIN与DeepEP，但其GPU-NIC边界性能缺乏系统剖析。作者梳理队列放置、请求构造、门铃排序与完成语义，并实现mini-gda和mini-proxy最小传输，在H100/H200/B200/GB200上与多种库对比。最小GPU路径发操作0.7μs、完成4.0μs，库最多增加4.6μs；共享队列可令延迟升1-3个数量级。该工作分离硬件机制与库开销，揭示提交路径不足以预测通信性能。
papers.abstract_en: GPU-initiated communication lets GPU threads post RDMA operations directly to the NIC. It underpins NVSHMEM, NCCL GIN, and DeepEP, which serve the fine-grained, latency-critical communication of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, yet its performance characteristics and optimizations remain scarcely documented beyond source code, and library comparisons fail to separate the costs of the hardware mechanism from those of the library around it.   This paper dissects GPU-initiated communication at the GPU-NIC boundary. We first detail the GPU-side network path: queue placement, work-request construction, doorbell ordering, and completion semantics. We then introduce mini-gda and mini-proxy, minimal transports for the GPU and CPU-proxy submission paths, and measure them alongside NVSHMEM IBGDA, NCCL GIN, DeepEP, UCCL-EP, MSCCL++, and fabric-lib on NVIDIA H100, H200, B200, and GB200 platforms. A minimal GPU path issues an operation in 0.7 $μ$s and completes in 4.0 $μ$s; libraries add up to 4.6 $μ$s of issue time through queue management, memory ordering, and completion scope, and issue time scales with the SM clock. A tuned CPU proxy matches or beats the GPU path at idle, at the cost of a dedicated core whose operating state sets its latency and throughput. On either path, sharing a queue with bulk traffic raises latency by one to three orders of magnitude. Reaching the 260 M msg/s ceiling of our InfiniBand platform requires doorbell batching and queue parallelism, and both have resource costs: communication code can reduce GPU block residency even when unused, and all-to-all traffic loses 59% of its NIC message rate at about 3,000 active connections. The submission path alone therefore does not predict communication performance. Our experiment code and results are available at https://github.com/ParCoreLab/Dissecting-GPU-Communication-Experiments.

papers.title_en: FastEEP: Fast Intra-Instance Elastic Scaling for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
papers.authors: Yunfei Feng, Jingkai He, Shiqi Liu, Cheng Zhang, Dong Du, Erhu Feng
papers.evidence: 专家并行MoE服务组的实例内弹性扩缩容
papers.tldr: MoE服务需随负载动态调整容量，但仅增删实例难以高效改变专家并行组，实例级扩缩容需销毁重建整个实例、开销大。FastEEP面向实例内弹性扩缩容，基于部分复用思想，将可复用执行结构与当前EP配置激活的资源分离，跨worker执行、GPU内存和通信复用运行时状态。评估中其扩缩容速度比基于vLLM的方案快4.5至11.7倍。该工作实现了无需整体拆除重建的快速细粒度MoE服务扩缩容。
papers.abstract_en: Large-scale expert parallelism (EP) has become the standard deployment configuration for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models in production. Meanwhile, the highly dynamic nature of LLM workloads requires providers to continuously adjust serving capacity to match fluctuating demand. Scaling MoE serving cannot be efficiently achieved by simply adding or removing serving instances; instead, it often requires resizing the EP group within an existing instance, which we refer to as intra-instance scaling.Existing inference engines primarily rely on instance-level scaling, which destroys and reconstructs entire serving instances, incurring substantial scaling overhead.   We present FastEEP (Fast Elastic Expert Parallel), a fast intra-instance scaling system for MoE serving based on the principle of Partial Reuse. FastEEP reuses existing runtime state across worker execution, GPU memory, and communication by separating reusable execution structures from the resources activated by the current EP configuration. This separation enables coordinated resource reclamation and reconfiguration while preserving costly-to-reconstruct state, allowing fast EP scaling without full instance teardown and reconstruction. Our evaluation shows that FastEEP achieves 4.5x--11.7x faster scaling than the existing vLLM-based approach across different models, enabling efficient, fine-grained scaling of MoE serving.

papers.title_en: Efficient CPU-GPU collaborative MoE inference via Adaptive Expert Assignment
papers.authors: Wenhui Lv, Yunming Liao, Hongli Xu, Yang Xu, Junhao Cheng
papers.evidence: 面向MoE推理的自适应专家分配与基于token负载的CPU-GPU平衡
papers.tldr: MoE 模型专家内存占用大，常超出 GPU 容量，需要把专家卸载到 CPU，但现有系统要么把未命中专家搬到 GPU 导致 PCIe 传输开销大，要么在 CPU 上执行使慢速 CPU 成为瓶颈。本文提出 CPU-GPU 协同推理系统，按专家 token 负载自适应分配：高负载专家传到 GPU，低负载专家留在 CPU，并动态调整分配以平衡两条执行路径。实验表明，prefill 速度最高提升 51.9%，decode 吞吐最高提升 39.5%。
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models reduce inference computation through sparse expert activation, but their large expert memory footprint often exceeds GPU capacity, making expert offloading necessary for memory-constrained inference. However, existing systems typically handle GPU-missed experts by either transferring them to the GPU, incurring substantial PCIe transfer latency, or executing them on the CPU, making the slower CPU computation the bottleneck. To address these limitations, we present \method, a CPU-GPU collaborative MoE inference system that adaptively assigns these missed experts to the CPU or GPU for efficient execution. By exploiting differences in expert token-loads, \method selectively transfers high-load experts to the GPU while executing low-load experts on the CPU. To minimize inference latency, \method adaptively adjusts expert assignments to balance the CPU computation path against the GPU transfer-and-computation path, allowing both execution paths to complete as early as possible. Extensive experiments on three representative MoE LLMs show that \method improves prefill speed by up to 51.9\% and decode throughput by up to 39.5\% over the strongest baseline across the evaluated batch sizes, with consistent gains under different GPU-memory budgets.

papers.title_en: Triple Overlap in Pipelined Krylov Methods on Multi-GPU Systems
papers.authors: Sinan Ekmekçibaşı, James D. Trotter, Johannes Langguth, Xing Cai, Didem Unat
papers.evidence: 借助集合通信库把计算通信重叠扩展为三重重叠
papers.tldr: 流水线 Krylov 方法常用于科学计算，但多 GPU 上计算与通信重叠仍不充分。本文提出三重重叠实现，将集合通信、不规则点对点通信与计算内核并发执行，覆盖 Pipe-PCG 与 Pipe-BiCGStab。在 MareNostrum 5 和 Leonardo 上，三流设计全面优于双流基线，64 GPU 时 Pipe-PCG 几何平均加速 1.33x/1.23x，大规模最高约 35% 和 33%，相对 PETSc 最高 3.27x。该工作扩展了通信重叠维度，并开源代码。
papers.abstract_en: We introduce a novel triple-overlap implementation of the pipelined preconditioned conjugate gradient (Pipe-PCG) and pipelined stabilized biconjugate gradient (Pipe-BiCGStab) solvers, methods widely used in scientific applications. By leveraging a collective communication library, our approach extends conventional computation-communication overlap to concurrently execute collective operations, irregular P2P communication, and compute kernels, enabling computation-communication-communication overlap across multiple GPUs. We evaluate the design on the MareNostrum 5 (H100) and Leonardo (A100) supercomputers, comparing against PETSc and the state-of-the-art two-stream NCCL implementation using SuiteSparse matrices and three massive instances scaled up to 512 GPUs. The three-stream design outperforms the two-stream baseline on every instance, with the margin widening from 2-6% at 4 GPUs to 18-47% at 64 GPUs. At 64 GPUs, the geometric-mean speedup over the two-stream baseline is 1.33x on MareNostrum 5 and 1.23x on Leonardo for Pipe-PCG, and reaches 1.30x for Pipe-BiCGStab. In large-scale experiments, we observed a speedup up to 35% in Pipe-PCG and up to 33% in Pipe-BiCGStab compared to the two-stream design. For PETSc, the margin is even wider, up to 3.27x speedup in both Pipe-PCG and Pipe-BiCGStab. Related code for the proposed method is available online: https://github.com/ParCoreLab/aCG
